posts.title: Fostering Inclusivity with the PostgreSQL Europe Diversity Committee
posts.description: As promised during the session, I'm sharing the slides from the "Fostering Inclusivity with the PostgreSQL Europe Diversity Committee" presentation at the New PostgreSQL Community Members - Summit at PostgreSQL Conference Europe (PGConf.EU) 2026 . The community day sessions weren't recorded, so there won't be a video of this one. I've made an attempt at a transcript to go with the slides! As with most people in the Postgres community, I wear multiple hats. In my day job, I’m a Senior Software Engineer at Snowflake. I talk about databases at Postgres events and at developer events to help spread the love for Postgres outside of the Postgres community. I’m on the org team for PGConf.EU. I chair the PostgreSQL Europe (PGEU) Diversity Committee. And I dream of "just quietly getting on with techie stuff"! posts.title: Tuning Postgres for Analytics - PGConf.EU
posts.description: Please enjoy the slides and transcript from Tuning Postgres for Analytics at PostgreSQL Conference Europe (PGConf.EU) in Valencia, Spain on 20 Oct 2026. I'll add a link to the recording once it's available. I've included just very brief alt-text for each slide image, but I've tried to add any links or other essential information into the body of the blog post. Obviously, I don't know the specifics of your particular Postgres environment. But, as always, there are some generalisations that apply to most systems. So, just for today, we're going to imagine that you're running a small chain of popular coffee shops in Valencia . If you've seen any of my previous talks, you might start to notice a coffee and cake theme in lots of my talks, demos and examples! You've implemented a state of the art system to manage your sales, stock, customer loyalty program etc. and you've carefully configured your production database for the needs of your day-to-day application workload. posts.title: How much do you really need to know about databases?
posts.description: Slides and transcript from How much do you really need to know about databases? at EuroPython 2026 in Kraków, Poland on 15 July 2026. I will add a link to the recording once it's available. I've included just very brief alt-text for each slide image, but I've also added any links or other essential information into the body of the blog post. This talk is aimed at application developers, whether or not you already have some database knowledge. And if that's not your profile, you're welcome in any case, because I'm always happy to talk about databases to anyone at all! So, let’s find out how much you really need to know about databases. Just to reassure you (because you may start to wonder as the talk goes on) that I really do have a life outside databases: this is a photo of me in my happy place, splattered in mud, out on my mountain bike in the French Alps, where I live.
